subject: Varying df across items with itemfit() function

messages.author: 9b6a77304b894501
messages.subject: Varying df across items with itemfit() function
parts:
I am calculating X2, G2, and S_X2, with sample size of several thousand. My question is, "Why does df vary from item to item?" I know the default is group.bins = 10, and many items have df = 8 (10 bins minus 2 parameters). However, some items have df as low as 4 (see attached example).

Also, when I use the empirical.plot option, the number of plotted points does not match df. For example, if df = 4, I might expect to see 6 plotted points (for a 2-parameter model). Is there a no connection between df and empirical.plot?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Varying df across items with itemfit() function
parts: Hi Jeffrey,

On Tue, Jun 2, 2020 at 5:30 PM Jeffrey Steedle <jtst...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am calculating X2, G2, and S_X2, with sample size of several thousand. My question is, "Why does df vary from item to item?" I know the default is group.bins = 10, and many items have df = 8 (10 bins minus 2 parameters). However, some items have df as low as 4 (see attached example).

Does your data contain a lot of missing observations? The organization in the itemfit() function currently does sorting and selection assuming no missing data, and then omits observations if they are missing row-wise, which could potentially reduce the df for X2 and G2.

Also, when I use the empirical.plot option, the number of plotted points does not match df. For example, if df = 4, I might expect to see 6 plotted points (for a 2-parameter model). Is there a no connection between df and empirical.plot?

This I'm not sure; you're correct the same df information should be plotted based on the internal computations of X2/G2. In any event, could you help me reproduce your two concerns with some code/data in case this behaviour should be patched? Cheers.

Phil

I'm sending a reproducible example with the data file attached (data_N448.csv)

I wanted to assess three versions of a CRT cognitive measure, the original 3-item measure and two longer versions - an 8-item version and 11-item version applying item response theory analyses (a two-parameter logistic model), to see whether the longer versions are appropriate for participants with both lower and higher levels of the latent trait.

#Model fit:

#        M2 df     p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95 SRMSR   TLI   CFI

Hi Jeffrey,

On Tue, Jun 2, 2020 at 5:30 PM Jeffrey Steedle <jtst...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am calculating X2, G2, and S_X2, with sample size of several thousand. My question is, "Why does df vary from item to item?" I know the default is group.bins = 10, and many items have df = 8 (10 bins minus 2 parameters). However, some items have df as low as 4 (see attached example).


Does your data contain a lot of missing observations? The organization in the itemfit() function currently does sorting and selection assuming no missing data, and then omits observations if they are missing row-wise, which could potentially reduce the df for X2 and G2. 
 

Also, when I use the empirical.plot option, the number of plotted points does not match df. For example, if df = 4, I might expect to see 6 plotted points (for a 2-parameter model). Is there a no connection between df and empirical.plot?

This I'm not sure; you're correct the same df information should be plotted based on the internal computations of X2/G2. In any event, could you help me reproduce your two concerns with some code/data in case this behaviour should be patched? Cheers.

Phil

On Thu, Nov 11, 2021 at 3:24 PM aniramfoggy <morni...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm sending a reproducible example with the data file attached (data_N448.csv)

I wanted to assess three versions of a CRT cognitive measure, the original 3-item measure and two longer versions - an 8-item version and 11-item version applying item response theory analyses (a two-parameter logistic model), to see whether the longer versions are appropriate for participants with both lower and higher levels of the latent trait.
All the items are binary with no missing values.
Sample size is 448.


#importing data
df.NA.zaCRT3 <- read_csv("data_N448.csv")
df.NA.zaCRT3 <- df.NA.zaCRT3[,-1]

psych::describe(df.NA.zaCRT3)
#Checking for missing values -> none are missing
colSums(is.na(df.NA.zaCRT3))

#selecting items and forming 3 data frames:
podaci.CRT.rec <- as.data.frame(dplyr::select(df.NA.zaCRT3, CRT1:CRT11)) #data frame with all the 11 items
podaci.CRT8.rec <- as.data.frame(dplyr::select(df.NA.zaCRT3, CRT1:CRT3, CRT5:CRT8,CRT11)) #data frame with 8 items

#Model fit:

Dana srijeda, 17. lipnja 2020. u 17:00:29 UTC+2 korisnik rphilip....@gmail.com napisao je:
Hi Jeffrey,

On Tue, Jun 2, 2020 at 5:30 PM Jeffrey Steedle <jtst...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am calculating X2, G2, and S_X2, with sample size of several thousand. My question is, "Why does df vary from item to item?" I know the default is group.bins = 10, and many items have df = 8 (10 bins minus 2 parameters). However, some items have df as low as 4 (see attached example).


Does your data contain a lot of missing observations? The organization in the itemfit() function currently does sorting and selection assuming no missing data, and then omits observations if they are missing row-wise, which could potentially reduce the df for X2 and G2. 
 

Also, when I use the empirical.plot option, the number of plotted points does not match df. For example, if df = 4, I might expect to see 6 plotted points (for a 2-parameter model). Is there a no connection between df and empirical.plot?

This I'm not sure; you're correct the same df information should be plotted based on the internal computations of X2/G2. In any event, could you help me reproduce your two concerns with some code/data in case this behaviour should be patched? Cheers.

Phil

df.S_X2 does vary across the items due to collapsing cells for the
expectation computations. You can fix the df to be constant, but it's
inadvisable.
